Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are marching toward the center and so are the players of Bangladesh. Ben Dawkins and Joe Moores will open the innings for England. Al Fahad is set to start with the new ball. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

England chasing 137 for victory - So, the target is 137 for the English batters and they have an easy task to chase the target, but the track looks something to offer the spinners. However, if Bangladeshi pacers get some openings in the first Powerplay, then the spinners might carry forward the momentum in the middle phase of the inning. Stick around with us as the second chapter of his contest will approx 11.05 am GMT.

Ralphie Albert of England Under-19 is up for chat - Albert starts off by praising the team's fielding, highlighting outstanding catches from Moores and Dawkins. He also commends the bowlers for their consistent lines and lengths, which he believes made the difference on a good pitch. Albert attributes his current success to bowling in partnership with Farhan, which has helped him pick up a few more wickets. He emphasizes that the team's bowling unit is performing well overall.

The wickets began to tumble like dominoes, and with each dismissal, Bangladesh's chances of building another substantial partnership faded. Just when the batters appeared settled, the English bowlers struck again, extinguishing the Bangladeshi innings and bundling them out for a mere 136 runs in just 39 overs. This decisive spell from the English spin attack shifted the momentum dramatically and highlighted the fragility of Bangladesh's batting under pressure.

English spinners spark dramatic collapse - After an initial setback in the very first over, Rifat Beg and skipper Azizul Hakim Tamim forged a formidable partnership that offered hope to Bangladesh. Rifat, taking the lead, faced the majority of the deliveries, searching for boundaries, while Azizul played a key supporting role by consistently rotating the strike to keep Rifat in the groove. However, just when it seemed that the Bangladeshi batters were firmly in control, the crafty English spin duo of Farhan Ahmed and Ralphie Albert broke through. In a stunning turnaround, they dismantled the burgeoning 46-run partnership and quickly added two more wickets to their tally, reducing Bangladesh from a promising 54-1 in the 11th over to a precarious 72-4 by the 19th over.

England Under19 Dominates With Ball - It has been another sensational inning from the bowling unit of England Under-19. In their previous match, they bundled Scotland for 152 runs and today it's even better as they have bundled Bangladesh for 136 runs. All the bowlers did their job, but Sebastian Morgan had a standout performance with the figure of 7-0-28-3.

Commentary.Commentary: All the pre-match formalities are done and the focus now shifts to cricket. The English team strides out in the middle, followed by the openers of Bangladesh Under-19. It is the duo of Rifat Beg and Zawad Abrar at the top for Bangladesh Under-19. Sebastian Morgan will be bowling the first over of this contest.
Both teams have walked out in the middle and have lined up on either sides of the match officials for their respective national anthems.

Thomas Rew, the England Under-19 captain, expressed his preference for batting first, citing the surface as looking very good. He mentioned that the team had a day off, with some players catching up on school work, followed by a couple of training sessions. Rew praised their opponents, highlighting their strong batting order and good bowling attack, and stated that they would stick to their usual game plan. He also announced a team change, with James Minto replacing Luke Hands.

Azizul Hakim Tamim, the Bangladesh Under-19 captain, stated that they will bat first due to the surface and conditions. He also praised the performance of the pace bowlers and batters, and mentioned that the team remains unchanged

Bangladesh Under-19 (Playing XI) - Rifat Beg, Zawad Abrar, Azizul Hakim Tamim (C), Kalam Siddiki Aleen, Rizan Hossan, Md Abdullah (WK), Samiun Basir Ratul, Shahriar Ahmed, Al Fahad, Iqbal Hossain, Shadin Islam.
England Under-19 (Playing XI) - Ben Dawkins, Joe Moores, Ben Mayes, Thomas Rew (C)(WK), Caleb Falconer, Ralphie Albert, Farhan Ahmed, Sebastian Morgan, James Minto, Manny Lumsden, Alex Green.
TOSS - Bangladesh Under-19 have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

Bangladesh Under-19, on the other hand, have navigated a path filled with high drama and showcased immense potential. Their encounter with the five-time champions, India Under-19, ended in heartbreak as a promising chase was derailed by a rain-induced collapse. After a wash-out against New Zealand Under-19, the Tigers roared back with a convincing win over the USA Under-19. This clash raises a fascinating tactical question, can the incisive, electric pace of the Bangladesh Under-19 seam attack penetrate and disrupt the momentum of the dashing England Under-19 batting lineup? The stage is set for a captivating encounter that could have major implications for both teams' semi-final prospects. Stay tuned for toss and team updates...

Thomas Rew's England side has been a force to be reckoned with so far. Their opening victory over Pakistan Under-19, where the bowlers successfully defended a modest total, demonstrated the team's resilience and mental fortitude. Clinical batting displays, led by the consistent form of Ben Mayes, Joe Moores and skipper Rew himself, ensured comfortable victories against Zimbabwe Under-19 and Scotland Under-19. The team's collective performance has marked them as a formidable contender in this championship, with all departments firing in unison, posing a significant challenge to any opposition they face in the Super 6 stage.

Welcome, cricket fans across the world, tuning in for a pivotal Super 6, Group 2 clash in the ICC Under-19 World Cup 2026, as Bangladesh Under-19 prepare to lock horns with England Under-19 at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo. This contest pits two of the tournament's most inspiring sides against each other, both having demonstrated significant quality in their respective group stages. England Under-19 arrive with an unblemished record, a perfect three wins from three encounters, showcasing a balanced attack and consistent batting lineup that has powered them through Group C. Meanwhile, Bangladesh Under-19 have displayed grit and flashes of brilliance in a challenging Group B, weathering the challenges posed by cricketing giants to earn their place at this crucial juncture of the tournament.
... MATCHDAY ...

The Super Six stage is well and truly underway, and the spotlight now shifts to Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo for a fascinating clash between England Under-19 and Bangladesh Under-19. England arrive with plenty of momentum after a dominant group stage, while Bangladesh know this is a massive opportunity to make a statement after showing both their quality and vulnerability in equal measure so far. England have looked one of the most complete side in the tournament, finishing top of their group with three convincing wins. Their batting has been led brilliantly by Ben Mayes, who produced one of the standout knocks of the competition with a stunning 191 against Scotland, which is the highest-ever individual score for an English batter at this level, while Thomas Rew and Joe Moores have provided solidity at the top. Caleb Falconer has also been impressive with his all-round skills, chipping in with crucial runs and wickets, showing composure under pressure. With the ball, England have shared the workload well, with Ralphie Albert, Manny Lumsden and Farhan Ahmed all contributing regularly, giving them depth and flexibility in their attack. Their biggest strength remains their ability to put up big totals and then apply relentless pressure with disciplined bowling. Bangladesh, on the other hand, finished second in their group with one win, one loss and a washout, but their performances suggest they are far more dangerous than the results indicate. They were in control for large parts against India before rain and some reckless shot selection cost them the game, which will still be fresh in their minds. Skipper Azizul Hakim Tamim has been their standout batter, scoring a couple of half-centuries in both completed games, while Zawad Abrar and Rifat Beg have offered support in the middle. With the ball, Al Fahad was excellent against India picking up a fantastic fifer, while Iqbal Hossain has been another key weapon, picking up important wickets including a match-winning spell against USA, and Rizan Hossan has been effective in providing control through the middle overs. The pitch at Queens Sports Club usually offers something for everyone. Batters who apply themselves early are rewarded, but there is enough movement for seamers, especially under cloud cover. Rain interruptions could once again bring the DLS method into play, making starts and momentum crucial for both sides. England will back their strong top order and balanced bowling unit, while Bangladesh will hope their spinners and in-form batters can exploit any pressure situations. With Super Six points on the line, this is not just about form, but about holding nerve when it matters most.
